The framework seeks to address buyer and financing concerns, while turning agricultural waste, cattle dung and other organic waste into energy.

items.summary: Chief Economic Adviser V Anantha Nageswaran said India will need greater private-capital participation to finance its development ambitions towards 2047, urging states to create an investment-friendly ecosystem and strengthen capital expenditure. At a two-day conference on financing Viksit Bharat, Nageswaran said, “Viksit Bharat depends on Viksit Rajya”, while discussions also focused on savings, agriculture, energy transition, technology and fiscal resilience.

items.title: Uday Kotak lays out 7 priorities for Viksit Bharat, warns against economic complacency
items.summary: Veteran banker Uday Kotak urged India to avoid complacency despite its strong global position, calling for tighter fiscal management, financial-sector reforms and stronger domestic production. Speaking at a Finance Ministry conference, Kotak outlined seven priorities for Viksit Bharat, including fiscal consolidation, reducing import dependence, addressing gold holdings and balancing regulation with economic growth.

items.title: Assam's revised ATISIS gives major boost to GTAC-linked CTC exports
items.summary: Assam's updated tea incentive scheme introduces exciting export benefits designed to enhance the quality of CTC tea. The initiative promises a Rs 3 per kg bonus for single-origin Assam tea exports and significantly boosts subsidies for Orthodox and Specialty tea production. Additionally, improved working capital assistance is provided, with Matcha tea now part of the program, aiming to fortify Assam's tea exports and the Guwahati auction platform.

items.title: Canada optimistic about concluding trade talks with India by year-end, minister says
items.summary: Canada anticipates finalizing a comprehensive economic partnership agreement with India by year's end. Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu expressed optimism regarding the upcoming negotiations and potential meetings. Discussions are focusing on the energy sector, including liquefied natural gas projects. Both nations are also exploring expanded cooperation in nuclear energy development. Indian firms are considering investments in Canada's critical mineral projects for supply chain security.

items.title: A costly policy error by China should be a cautionary tale for India
items.summary: India’s fertility rate has fallen below replacement level, prompting an EAC-PM working paper to argue that population control should no longer be a policy goal. Pointing to China’s difficulty reversing decades of low fertility, the paper says India should phase out sterilisation-linked incentives and two-child norms while retaining access to contraception and reproductive healthcare.
